items.reason: Licence confirmed CC BY 2.0 with a passed Flickr review. Real photograph, no watermark or border, sharp. items.whatItShows: Symmetrical one-point-perspective view down the aisle between two rows of Frontier supercomputer cabinets at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. Two large matte-black end panels face the camera; the left one carries white Oak Ridge / U.S. Department of Energy / Hewlett Packard Enterprise / AMD logos, the right one the FRONTIER wordmark and compass emblem. A bright perforated-tile floor runs between them to a vanishing point; fluorescent strips and cable trays overhead.
items.subjectRegion: Two black panels fill roughly x 5-38% and x 58-92%, y 22-92%. The aisle and vanishing point are dead centre (x 38-58%), vanishing at about 55% height.
items.negativeSpace: The lower halves of both black end panels (below the logos, y 62-92%) are clean, flat near-black areas; the right panel is quieter than the left because it has only one emblem. The bottom 8% is plain white floor. The top 22% (ceiling) is busy.
items.depthStructure: Strong and readable: white floor foreground, the two end panels as a near plane, then cabinet sides and cabling receding along the aisle to a far wall about 30 m back, with the ceiling receding in parallel. Clear near/far separation in the centre, but the two panels themselves are flat planes.
items.tonalNotes: Very high contrast, close to a two-tone image: panels and cabinet interiors near black, floor, ceiling lights and logos near white. Median luminance 85/255, full range used. Converts to grayscale with no loss.
items.cropAdvice: Only 1920 px wide (the 3000x1992 original could not be fetched), so use at up to roughly full-HD width or expect upscaling. Keep the crop symmetrical; a tall centre crop of the aisle alone (x 35-62%) also works and removes most logos.
items.attribution: OLCF at ORNL (Oak Ridge Leadership Computing Facility), "Frontier Supercomputer", 2022, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0

items.whatItShows: A long row of black IBM Summit supercomputer cabinets at Oak Ridge National Laboratory seen at a steep angle. The near end panel carries the vertical 'summit' wordmark and a pale angular chevron graphic, with Oak Ridge and IBM logos above; the cabinet fronts with faceted grey chevron doors recede to the right. Pale cooling ducts, black hoses and cable trays run overhead; a bright floor strip lies at far right.
items.subjectRegion: The near cabinet end fills x 14-52%, y 16-100%; the row of cabinet fronts recedes from x 52% to a vanishing area at about x 96%, y 40%. Subject mass is the whole lower-left three quarters of the frame.
items.negativeSpace: The black end panel between the 'summit' wordmark and the cabinet edge (x 30-50%, y 35-100%) is a large near-black area, interrupted only by the pale chevron at x 22-32%. The far-left strip (x 0-13%) is a dark mesh door. The bright floor wedge at bottom right (x 82-100%, y 50-100%) is the only quiet light area.
items.depthStructure: Excellent: near end panel as foreground, cabinet fronts shrinking continuously into the distance on a strong diagonal, overhead pipes receding in parallel, and a blurred bright far end of the hall. Continuous depth gradient from left (near) to right (far).
items.tonalNotes: Dark-dominant: median luminance 44/255. Deep blacks in the cabinets, mid-greys in the chevron doors, highlights in the overhead ducts and the floor at right. Already almost monochrome in colour.
items.cropAdvice: 16:9 as supplied. Text is best placed over the black end panel at left-centre; avoid cropping the right edge or the perspective loses its vanishing point.
items.attribution: Carlos Jones / Oak Ridge National Laboratory, "Summit supercomputer", 2018, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0

items.whatItShows: Oblique close view along a row of black server racks in a dark data centre (Wikimedia Foundation servers, 2012). Stacks of 1U Dell servers with drive bays and vent grilles catch the light; the rack in the centre is in sharp focus, the one at far right is large and blurred in the foreground, and further racks recede into darkness at left.
items.subjectRegion: Sharp, bright rack of servers at centre (x 42-60%, y 12-100%); a second lighter rack at x 26-35%; a large out-of-focus rack fills the right edge (x 78-100%, full height).
items.negativeSpace: A solid black vertical band between the centre rack and the right foreground rack (x 62-77%, full height) is the cleanest text area. The left third (x 0-25%) is dark and low-detail, fading to a blurred ceiling at top left. Several narrower black rack posts run the full height.
items.depthStructure: Three clear layers from shallow depth of field: blurred near rack at right, sharp middle rack at centre, racks receding and dimming to the left background. Very good depth separation for a point cloud.
items.tonalNotes: Dark-dominant: median luminance 31/255, with true blacks covering more than a third of the frame and specular highlights on the server faces. Low colour content in the original, so the grayscale version loses nothing.
items.cropAdvice: Works full-bleed at 3:2. For a vertical crop take x 40-80% to keep the sharp rack and the black band. Do not crop the right foreground rack entirely or the depth cue is lost.
items.attribution: Victor Grigas (Victorgrigas), "Wikimedia Foundation Servers-8055 10", 2012, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0

items.whatItShows: Elevated wide view across the CERN computing centre machine hall in 2009: many rows of grey open-topped server racks with glass or mesh tops fill the floor, a slatted luminous ceiling fills the upper third, and a tiled wall with numbered bays (30 to 70) runs across the middle. Shot through a window from a gallery, so there are faint reflections.
items.subjectRegion: Racks fill the lower 60% of the frame edge to edge, with the largest block at lower left to centre (x 3-72%, y 60-100%). The ceiling occupies y 0-30%, the wall y 30-48%.
items.negativeSpace: No truly dark or empty area. The tiled back wall (x 18-100%, y 32-46%) is the most even band, in mid-grey. Text placed anywhere else will sit on busy texture.
items.depthStructure: Good scale recession: near racks at the bottom, rows stepping back to the far wall, with the ceiling slats converging the same way. Depth is continuous but texture is uniformly busy, so layers do not separate cleanly.
items.tonalNotes: Mid-toned and busy: median luminance 95/255, bright ceiling panels and reflections on rack tops, few real blacks. Looks heavily contrast-processed, with halo-like glare under the wall lights and wavy reflections on the rack tops.
items.cropAdvice: Best used small or as a wide strip cropped to y 40-100% to drop the ceiling. Not strong enough to carry a full-bleed section.
items.attribution: Florian Hirzinger (www.fh-ap.com), "CERN Server 03", 2009, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0

items.whatItShows: Focus-stacked macro of an Nvidia GA102 graphics processor (GeForce RTX 3090) soldered to its board, seen at a three-quarter angle. The bare silicon die, laser-etched 'NVIDIA / S TW 2032A1 / SNNB9W.000 / GA102-300-A1', sits in a dark substrate ringed by rows of tiny capacitors, inside a pale metal stiffener frame; dark memory chips surround it at the edges.
items.subjectRegion: The die is centred (x 18-82%, y 18-76%) and the pale frame around it fills nearly the whole image (x 0-100%, y 8-95%) as a rotated square. Dark memory chips sit in the four corners.
items.negativeSpace: There is no dark quiet zone large enough for text. The smooth die surface (centre) and the pale frame (a broad band lower left and upper right) are quiet but light, so text there would need to be dark. The corners are dark but textured with chip markings.
items.depthStructure: Shallow physical relief only: board and memory chips, the raised frame, the recessed substrate, and the die standing proud. Depth is real but a few millimetres; expect a gentle relief with strong edges rather than layered recession.
items.tonalNotes: Light-dominant: median luminance 181/255. Pale frame and die against dark chips and substrate, with crisp edge contrast and fine detail. The original is nearly neutral in colour.
items.cropAdvice: Fill the frame with it. A square crop centred on the die (x 18-82%) is strong. Avoid enlarging beyond native size: the fine capacitor rows alias when scaled badly.
items.attribution: Fritzchens Fritz, "Nvidia GA102 (GeForce RTX 3090) GPU die", 2020, via Wikimedia Commons, CC0 1.0 (attribution not required, given as courtesy)

items.whatItShows: An Nvidia HGX B200 eight-GPU Blackwell baseboard on a wooden table: two rows of four tall black finned heatsink towers with polished silver tops bearing the NVIDIA logo, a small white card reading 'HGX B200 NVL8' on top, power connectors and voltage regulators along the near edge. Workshop clutter and a metal chassis in the background.
items.subjectRegion: The board fills almost the whole frame (x 3-97%, y 5-95%). The near row of four heatsinks is the main mass at x 5-80%, y 18-70%; the label card is at x 44-55%, y 10-18%.
items.negativeSpace: None usable. The heatsink fin faces (x 5-78%, y 35-65%) are dark but finely ribbed. The top-left corner is a grey metal panel and the bottom-left corner is pale table.
items.depthStructure: Moderate: connectors at the front, the near row of towers, the far row behind, then a cluttered background. The object has real volume, but the snapshot's deep focus and messy backdrop give little clean separation.
items.tonalNotes: Dark object on mid-grey surroundings: median luminance 77/255, blacks in the fins, highlights on the silver heatsink tops. Flat phone-style lighting.
items.cropAdvice: Use only as a small inset or cut out from its background. Nearly square (1920x1948), so it does not suit a wide band.

items.whatItShows: A full silicon wafer of Intel 4th-generation Core processor dies, photographed face-on as a near-perfect disc on a pure black background. The grid of rectangular dies is tilted about 20 degrees, with diagonal bands of light and shadow sweeping across it.
items.subjectRegion: A single disc, centred, x 19-84%, y 3-97% (it nearly touches the top and bottom edges).
items.negativeSpace: Pure black on both sides: left x 0-18% and right x 85-100%, full height, plus the four corners. Clean, true black, ideal for text.
items.depthStructure: Essentially flat: one planar disc against an empty background. A depth model will give a plate floating in front of nothing; any relief will come from the light bands, not real geometry.
items.tonalNotes: Extreme: more than half the pixels are pure black (median luminance 1/255), the wafer runs from dark grey to about 200/255 with no clipped highlights. Loses its iridescent colour in grayscale but keeps the banding.
items.cropAdvice: The disc is tight to the top and bottom edges, so add black canvas rather than cropping if more margin is needed; the background is uniform black and extends seamlessly. Works well as a circle bleeding off one side.
items.attribution: Intel in Deutschland, "4th Generation Intel Core Processor Wafer", 2013, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 2.0

items.whatItShows: Native black-and-white photograph looking straight down a 230 kV transmission corridor in Virginia Beach. Twin-pole H-frame pylons recede in one-point perspective between two dark tree lines; conductors fan out from the top edge of the frame down to the first pylon; heavy overcast sky above, pale dry grass and a light gravel strip below, a wooden fence at lower right.
items.subjectRegion: The first pylon stands just right of centre (x 39-58%, y 19-81%) with the receding pylons nested inside it down to a vanishing point at about x 48%, y 75%. Tree masses fill the left (x 0-40%, y 10-80%) and right (x 55-100%, y 40-82%).
items.negativeSpace: The sky: a broad mid-to-dark grey area at upper left (x 0-40%, y 0-25%) and a larger one at upper right (x 62-100%, y 0-38%), crossed only by thin wires near the centre. The bottom strip (y 90-100%) is light gravel.
items.depthStructure: Very good: gravel and bright grass in the foreground, the first pylon in the near middle distance, at least five further pylons shrinking to the vanishing point, tree lines converging on both sides, sky behind. Thin wires and bare branches will be hard for a depth model and may fragment.
items.tonalNotes: Full, balanced range without clipping: median luminance 109/255, pylons and left trees near black, grass and lower sky the lightest areas. Already a single-channel grayscale file with a deliberate monochrome grade.
items.cropAdvice: Wide 1.7:1 as supplied; the 8255 px original is available if more resolution is needed. Keep the top edge, since the wires entering from it make the composition. A centre vertical crop (x 28-70%) holds up.
items.attribution: PumpkinSky, "Power lines during Blue Hour BW", 2017, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0

items.whatItShows: 208-second night exposure of the coal-fired Rostock power station in Germany. A floodlit hyperbolic cooling tower at left sends a long smeared steam plume diagonally up and across a black sky; the tall blocky boiler house stands at centre with antenna masts on its roof; three street lamps with starbursts at right, lit plant buildings and car light trails along a road in the foreground.
items.subjectRegion: Cooling tower at left (x 7-23%, y 39-77%), boiler house at centre (x 35-56%, y 31-78%). The plume runs from the tower top at x 10%, y 39% diagonally to the top edge around x 30-75%. Street lamps at x 63%, 82% and 94%, y 57-69%.
items.negativeSpace: Black sky at top left (x 0-25%, y 0-33%) and a large black area at right (x 58-100%, y 0-52%) are true, clean blacks. The foreground road and grass (y 88-100%) are dark and quiet.
items.depthStructure: Good layering: dark grass and road in front, lamps and signs in the near middle distance, boiler house and tower behind, plume and sky as backdrop. The soft plume and starbursts have no real geometry and will read as flat or noisy depth; the buildings will separate well.
items.tonalNotes: Low-key with real blacks and bright accents: median luminance 50/255, tower and plume are the main highlight mass, lamps clip to white. Original is orange and brown; it converts to grayscale very well.
items.cropAdvice: Works full-bleed at 3:2. Text belongs in the black upper right. A left-weighted crop (x 0-60%) isolates tower, plume and boiler house as a vertical plate.
items.attribution: Radomianin, "Rostock Power Station, SW view", 2021, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0

items.whatItShows: Wide-angle drone view at sunset of the Google data centre in Council Bluffs, Iowa. One very long, low, pale-roofed hall runs diagonally from lower left to upper right, with a row of cooling units and tanks along its near side and a perimeter road curving round it. Flat farmland, a lake at upper left, bare trees at lower right, and the sun on the horizon at upper right under a banded sky.
items.subjectRegion: The building runs diagonally through the centre, from x 27%, y 52% to x 80%, y 35%, with the cooling plant along its lower-right side out to x 88%, y 75%. The horizon sits at y 21%.
items.negativeSpace: Dark grass and earth at lower left (x 0-28%, y 55-100%) and the dark tree mass at lower right (x 65-100%, y 70-100%) are low-detail. The upper-left sky (x 0-55%, y 0-18%) is a soft mid-grey.
items.depthStructure: Aerial recession: trees and embankment near, the building and loop road in the middle, farmland, lake and highway out to a far horizon, then sky. Depth is continuous and shallow-looking from this height; expect a tilted plane rather than distinct layers.
items.tonalNotes: Mid-to-dark and fairly flat on the ground: median luminance 83/255, no deep blacks (1st percentile 27/255), with a blown patch around the sun at upper right. Needs a contrast curve to work in black and white; the roof is the only bright ground element.
items.cropAdvice: Crop to the lower three quarters to remove the blown sun, or centre on the building at about 2:1. Drone wide-angle distortion bends the horizon slightly; avoid placing straight rules next to it.
items.attribution: Chad Davis, "Google Data Center, Council Bluffs Iowa", 2017, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0
